limitations: Reviewed Linux AMD64 server and required infrastructure image bytes only; no containers or services are created or started.
The upstream Compose file is provenance, not an activation template: mutable tags, public ports and CHANGEME credentials must not be applied verbatim.
Activation requires an owning Zone, private secrets, scoped durable volumes, backups, capacity, internal networking and an explicitly accepted UI access route.
No organization, user, project, API key, database schema or migration is created by software installation.

Hermes requires its actual runtime Langfuse SDK plus the opt-in observability/langfuse plugin and explicit per-profile endpoint/project credentials; missing SDK or credentials silently disables tracing.
Use metadata-only capture until scoped content-export approval; sanitization is not a guarantee against client data leakage.
Readiness requires healthy dependencies and a synthetic Hermes trace visible in the correct Langfuse project after flush, plus cross-Zone denial checks.
The MinIO version field records the published image creation timestamp, not an inferred upstream semantic version; its exact image bytes are pinned by digest.
